issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s use of a statutory claims process for property acquired by the State does not extinguish the mortgagee’s ordinary-law remedies against other mortgaged property outside that process.
material_facts: The mortgage covered both properties that vested in the State and properties that did not.
The mortgagee filed a claim under the statutory process, and the claims officer partly allowed it.
The mortgagee sought to withdraw the claim so that he could pursue remedies under ordinary law against the properties that had not vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee was not required to elect between the statutory process for the vested properties and ordinary-law remedies for the non-vested properties. Filing the statutory claim did not take away the right to pursue ordinary-law remedies against the non-vested properties. Any later enforcement against those properties may require application of the principle of marshalling.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 14, 4(d) and 35 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, the statutory authorities’ jurisdiction and the related restrictions concern claims and adjudications relating to property vested in the State; they do not bar ordinary-law remedies against property outside the Act. Raja Sailendra Narayan Bhanj Deo v. Kumar Jagat Kishore Prasad Narayan Singh and Krishna Prasad v. Gauri Kumari Devi concerned property wholly within the Act’s scope and do not decide the position where a mortgage covers both vested and non-vested property. The contrary election observations in Sukhdeo Das v. Kashi Prasad and Siddheshwar Prasad v. Ram Saroop were disapproved.

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_dispute: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a mortgage.
predicates.mortgage_covers_state_acquired_and_other: The mortgage covers both property acquired by the State and property outside that acquisition.
predicates.creditor_filed_claim_for_state_acquired_: The creditor submitted a claim through the special process for the property acquired by the State.
predicates.ordinary_remedy_remains_available_agains: The creditor may pursue an ordinary-law remedy against the mortgaged property outside the State acquisition.

issues.definition: When a mortgage-enforcement dispute concerns a mortgage covering both State-acquired and other property and the creditor filed a claim for the State-acquired property, the creditor retains an ordinary-law remedy against the other property.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal may permit withdrawal of a statutory claim when the request is limited to pursuing a remedy against property outside the statutory process and withdrawal would not prejudice the opposing party.
material_facts: The mortgagee asked the Board to permit withdrawal of his claim before the claims officer so he could pursue any available remedy against the mortgaged properties that had not vested in the State.
The request was made while the respondents’ appeal from the claims officer’s decision was before the Board.
The Board had refused withdrawal on the basis that filing the claim amounted to an election of remedies.
The Supreme Court found no positive prejudice to the respondents from allowing the limited withdrawal.
issues.conclusion: The request to withdraw the claim was allowed. Although Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure did not technically apply, there was no bar to the tribunal permitting withdrawal in the circumstances. The withdrawal was limited to enabling recourse against the non-vested properties; the Court expressed no opinion on the merits of the underlying claims. Any later enforcement against those properties may require application of the principle of marshalling.
issues.legal_principle: Even where Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure does not technically apply, a tribunal may permit withdrawal of a proceeding if satisfied that it can properly do so, and may consider whether withdrawal would prejudice the opposing party. Because the statutory process concerned only property vested in the State, the mistaken view that the creditor had elected an exclusive remedy could not justify refusing withdrawal of a claim for the limited purpose of pursuing a remedy against other property.

predicates.special_claim_proceeding: The proceeding is a claim before a special authority for adjudication of a creditor’s claim relating to property acquired by the State.
predicates.withdrawal_requested_only_to_pursue_reme: The creditor requested withdrawal solely to pursue a remedy against property outside the special process.
predicates.withdrawal_causes_no_prejudice: Allowing withdrawal would not positively prejudice the opposing party.
predicates.special_claim_may_be_withdrawn: The tribunal may permit withdrawal of the special claim.

issues.definition: A special claim may be withdrawn when withdrawal is sought only to pursue a remedy against other property and does not prejudice the opposing party.
